observations.content:
Summary: AlphaFold is an artificial intelligence system developed by Google DeepMind that predicts a protein’s 3D structure directly from its amino acid sequence. The system was created by the research lab Google DeepMind and has been recognized for its groundbreaking accuracy and speed in protein structure prediction, earning a share of the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry. AlphaFold has predicted the shapes of more than 200 million proteins and made them freely available to researchers around the world.

    AlphaFold is an artificial intelligence system, developed by the research lab Google DeepMind, that predicts a protein’s 3D structure directly from its amino acid sequence. In practical terms, it does in hours what used to take a laboratory months or years, and it does so with a level of accuracy that surprised even longtime experts in the field. [...] AlphaFold is an artificial intelligence system from Google DeepMind that predicts a protein’s 3D shape from its amino acid sequence, solving a problem that had challenged biology for roughly 50 years.
 The breakthrough was significant enough to earn a share of the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
 AlphaFold has predicted the shapes of more than 200 million proteins and made them freely available to researchers around the world. [...] AlphaFold is an artificial intelligence system from Google DeepMind that predicts the 3D shape of a protein from its amino acid sequence. Because a protein’s shape determines its function, this helps scientists understand how proteins work and how diseases might be treated. It solved a problem that had challenged biology for roughly 50 years.

observations.content:
Summary: AlphaFold is an artificial intelligence program developed by DeepMind, a subsidiary of Alphabet, which uses deep learning techniques to predict protein structures. Announced on 8 May 2024, AlphaFold 3 was co-developed by Google DeepMind and Isomorphic Labs, both subsidiaries of Alphabet. AlphaFold 3 can predict the structures of protein complexes with DNA, RNA, post-translational modifications, and selected ligands and ions. The AlphaFold Protein Structure Database, created by Google DeepMind and EMBL’s European Bioinformatics Institute (EMBL-EBI), provides over 200 million entries, offering broad coverage of UniProt.

observations.content:
Summary: The AlphaFold paper was published in Nature on 15 July 2021, titled "Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold" by DeepMind. The paper detailed the methodology behind AlphaFold and was cited over 40,000 times in scientific journals as of November 2025. The paper was accompanied by the release of the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database, which provided free access to predicted structures of the entire human proteome and 20 other model organisms, totaling over 350,000 structures. The methodology was recognized as a solution to the 50-year-old "protein folding problem" by the organizers of CASP14.

[1] AlphaFold — Google DeepMind
    https://deepmind.google/science/alphafold
    Nature publishes AlphaFold’s detailed methodology in the paper “Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold” and DeepMind open sources the code along with 60 pages of supplemental information. To-date, the paper has been cited over 40,000 times in scientific journals.

22nd July 2021

### We launch the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database with EMBL-EB [...] AlphaFold2 wins CASP14 by a huge margin and is recognised as a solution to the 50-year-old “protein folding problem” by the organisers of CASP after predicting structures down to atomic accuracy with a median error (RMSD\_95) of less than 1 Angstrom - 3 times more accurate than the next best system and comparable to experimental methods.

15th July 2021

### AlphaFold’s methodology is published in Nature [...] A week later, Nature publishes a second DeepMind paper containing the structure predictions of the entire human proteome. In close collaboration with the European Bioinformatics Institute at the European Molecular Biology Laboratory (EMBL-EBI), DeepMind launches the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database (AFDB) to give the scientific community free of charge and open access to the human proteome along with another 20 model organisms - over 350,000 structures in total.

28th July 2022
